design.quote: Patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction were randomized to receive placebo or empagliflozin 10 mg daily.

population.quote: Patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction were randomized to receive placebo or empagliflozin 10 mg daily.

sample_size.quote: A total of 5,988 patients were included.

intervention.quote: Patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction were randomized to receive placebo or empagliflozin 10 mg daily.

comparator.quote: Patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction were randomized to receive placebo or empagliflozin 10 mg daily.

follow_up.quote: The median follow-up time was 26.2 months.

primary_findings.quote: Empagliflozin (vs placebo) was associated with a more pronounced reduction of primary outcome events at higher baseline magnesium levels: Q1, HR: 1.05 [95% CI: 0.77-1.39]; Q2, HR: 0.85 [95% CI: 0.63-1.14]; Q3, HR: 0.88 [95% CI: 0.66-1.17]; Q4, HR: 0.62 [95% CI: 0.45-0.86]; Q5, HR: 0.60 [95% CI: 0.45-0.79]; interaction P-trend = 0.030.
primary_findings.outcome: composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization

primary_findings.quote: At week 4, empagliflozin had increased magnesium levels by 0.05 mmol/L, reaching a steady state thereafter.
